blocks.text: Most municipal GIS maps follow a similar logic. Start with the parcel layer — the solid lines showing lot boundaries. Click a parcel and you'll typically get an info window with the address, lot size, and PID.

parts.t: Then turn on the layers that matter: zoning (what's allowed to be built), OCP (what the city wants the area to become), ALR (whether it's protected farmland), flood plain, and any environmentally sensitive area overlays.
Watch for setbacks and easements — they shrink the buildable area on a lot, sometimes a lot. A 10,000 square foot lot with a 30-foot riparian setback isn't really 10,000 buildable.
If something looks off, call the city's planning department. Most are surprisingly helpful.
